grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; none of Rules A–F applies.
grade.summary: The proof is complete and correct. The lexicographic behavior of the number of entries greater than 1 and the integer-valued sum-of-squares potential proves termination, while the primewise gcd of all valuations is invariant and reconstructs the unique terminal entry.
strengths: Correctly computes the valuation transformation as (x,y) -> (min(x,y), |x-y|).
Provides a valid termination argument: the number of non-unit entries never increases, and whenever it stays constant the nonnegative integer potential strictly decreases.
Correctly proves that at least one entry remains greater than 1, hence a terminal board has exactly one such entry.
Correctly identifies and proves the primewise gcd invariants and derives an explicit formula for M depending only on the initial board.
